attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as the L3 forwarding router between node2 and node3. This required first building the missing point-to-point transit links (node1's eth1/eth2 had no IPs; node2/node3's second NIC enp8s0 was stuck waiting on DHCP that never arrives on this dhcp:false network). Assigned static addressing (node1 eth1=172.20.1.1/24 to node2 enp8s0=172.20.1.2/24; node1 eth2=172.20.2.1/24 to node3 enp8s0=172.20.2.2/24), added persistent routes on node2/node3 via nmcli, enabled IP forwarding on node1, and added an nftables FORWARD-hook table (inet transit_acl) that rejects tcp/23 with a TCP reset and explicitly accepts tcp/8080, leaving the default-accept policy untouched for all other traffic. Diagnosed and opened firewalld's local tcp/8080 port on node2 and node3 (their own host firewalls, not node1's ACL, were initially rejecting 8080 with an ICMP admin-prohibited reject from the destination host). Persisted node1's addressing/forwarding/ACL via a new systemd unit (transit-acl.service) since SONiC's own interfaces file only manages eth0. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot IDs plus working ACL/connectivity) on all three nodes, restarted each one at a time, polled until each came back, confirmed each boot_id changed, and re-verified full recovery of addressing, forwarding, the nftables ACL, and end-to-end TCP 8080/23 behavior plus untouched ICMP traffic in both directions.
